tasks-protected-rejection-in-the-lean-mo.text: Tasks: protected rejection in the Lean model.

Tasks are grouped by slice and named by what they achieve. A task is checked only by the ticket owner, after the slice is accepted, in the commit that stamps the slice. Each task names the requirements of the specification it serves. The gate is the proof; no task adds a check of its own.

story.text: As the coder given a slice, I read the tasks of that slice as the whole of my work and the terminal condition at its end as the only reason to stop, so that I neither stop early nor wander into a neighbouring ticket.

slice-one-one-booked-clock.text: [x] booked-time-on-request — a request records its booked submission time, serialized, zero when absent from older input. (one-booked-clock)
[x] window-reads-booked-time — the retraction window, its admission and the restated window statements read the request's time and ignore the witness's legacy field. (one-booked-clock)

[x] retract-question-carries-booked-time — the transport and the harness give a retraction question the booked time read from the request datum; a fold question is unchanged. (one-booked-clock, admission-changes-no-effect)
[x] protocol-seven — the driver's protocol version moves to 7 and the surface digest pin follows. (consumers-state-the-rule)

[x] regenerate-after-slice-one — corpora, theorem register and digests, simulator mirror, application corpus and the coverage record are regenerated from the model, with a published restatement table for every changed identity. (consumers-state-the-rule, unmet-stays-unmet)
[x] amendment-opened — constitution version 1.18.0 (taken after the fold lane's 1.16.0 and 1.17.0) is opened with the retraction row restated. (consumers-state-the-rule)
Terminal condition: every command of slice one's gate exits as the gate states, on a clean committed head; or a question is filed; or capacity is reached with a handoff.

slice-two-rejection-needs-evidence.text: [x] historical-scenario-accepted-on-base — the unguarded-rejection scenario is ported to the base API and run against the base model before any change; it reports the rejection accepted. This is the failing control. (rejection-needs-evidence, foldable-request-is-protected)
[x] registry-identity — a configuration and a request carry the abstract registry identity; every step preserves it. (evidence-is-bound)
[x] evidence-types — reason, evidence and witness exist as the data model states them. (evidence-is-bound, two-grounds-only)
[x] rejection-admission — admission refuses in the stated order and admits exactly the two grounds; the exit admission takes the state. (all requirements of rejection)
[x] rejection-statements — the statements named in the functions model for this slice are stated and proved over the two-edge model. (every requirement named there)
[x] all-reject-batch-witnesses — an all-reject batch carries one witness per request and one shared interval and judges each request in order. (batch-judged-action-by-action)

[x] rejection-corpus — the corpus exports the truth table cell by cell for the two admitted edges, one row per excluded tag, the three time positions, each refusal reason, unknown against Absent, and the historical scenario. (consumers-state-the-rule)
[x] historical-scenario-refused-after — the same scenario against the changed model reports the rejection refused. (foldable-request-is-protected)
[x] transport-decodes-evidence — a rejection question without its booked metadata is refused at decode; evidence attached to another exit is refused. (evidence-is-bound)
[x] harness-supplies-evidence — the harness allocates the registry identity while acting, reads the booked time from the request datum, and builds expiry and mismatch evidence. (evidence-is-bound)
[x] lawful-rows-rebased — the running book, the refund controls, the generic rows and the batch harness place their rejects after both windows with expiry evidence. (unmet-stays-unmet)
[x] amendment-reject-row — the rejection row, the outcome-class row and the reconciliation are restated. (consumers-state-the-rule)
Terminal condition as slice one. The in-window row is expected red at this head and is slice three.

slice-three-the-in-window-rows.text: [x] in-window-rows-per-ruling — the dedicated early-rejection row and the generic session's standing unmet row, with their workflow assertions, say what decision B directs: the dedicated row becomes a lawful mismatch rejection that both sides accept inside the windows; the unmet row books a foldable insertActive request for a key not yet registered and records its three steps as the divergences they now are, so that it stops matching the day the chain refuses. (unmet-stays-unmet)

[x] consumer-record-updated — the consumer conformance record, the book and the evidence page say the same, including the history of ticket 320's early rejection, without editing the history itself. (unmet-stays-unmet)
Terminal condition as slice one. The slice follows decision B and is independent of slice four.

slice-four-mixed-batches.text: Withdrawn on 14 October 2026, with the economic design: a rejection never spends the registry state output and never shares a transaction with a fold, so no batch holds both. Its tasks stay unchecked and are not done; the protection of a fold against a rejection ordered before it is statement 3 of the economics plan, carried by slice eight.
[ ] action-engine — the ordered action engine exists and the all-reject batch runs on it, the slice-two loop deleted in the same change. (batch-judged-action-by-action)
[ ] mixed-batch — the mixed-batch function refuses an empty batch, an empty interval and a net-mint mismatch. (batch-judged-action-by-action)
[ ] batch-statements — the batch statements named in the functions model are stated and proved. (batch-judged-action-by-action, foldable-request-is-protected)

[ ] mixed-batch-question — the driver's mixed-batch question, its corpus rows (fold then reject of the same fresh key accepted, the reverse refused, an empty batch refused) and the transport support. (consumers-state-the-rule)
[ ] amendment-completed — the mixed-batch row is added and the 1.18.0 entry is complete. (consumers-state-the-rule)

slices-five-to-ten-the-economic-model.text: Slices five to ten: the economic model.

Planned in the economics plan on the decided design; started after the plan is cleared; run in place of the withdrawn slice four, by the operator's order of 13 October 2026. The paper is not a slice of this list: it is written afterwards, from the finished model. Every slice begins with its failing controls and ends with the list of its statements, each with its fully qualified name and its axiom line.

slice-five-parameters-and-the-transactio.text: Slice five: parameters and the transaction vocabulary.
[x] failing-controls-five — a fold that changes a parameter, a reference to a spent output and an unbalanced transaction fail on the branch as it stands, for the intended reason.

[x] registry-parameters — the registration cost, minimum tip and maximum booking width exist in the configuration, default to zero in old input and are preserved by every fold; the width is below the processing window.

[x] transaction-vocabulary — output references and the unspent set, reference inputs, the validity interval, the fee and the donation (a zero donation omitted), the exact state token identity and the balance relation exist.
[x] statements-five — statement 1 and the supporting statements of the plan are proved from the standard axioms.
[x] protocol-eight — the driver protocol version moves where a declared question changed and the surface digest follows; no declared question changed, so the version stays.
[x] regenerate-after-slice-five — corpora, register and digests, theorem page, simulator mirror, application corpus, coverage record and restatement table follow. (consumers-state-the-rule)
[x] names-and-receipts-five — the slice's statements are listed with fully qualified name and axiom line at the final revision.

[x] built-form-repair — after the hosted conformance rows refused a built fold transaction that gained a field, the state token identity is written only when it differs from the registry default and is read back as the default when absent; the transaction rows of every scenario at the pre-slice-five baseline are byte-identical, kept by a committed baseline and a check that the model check runs. (consumers-state-the-rule)

slice-five-b-review-and-improvement-of-t.text: Slice five-b: review and improvement of the Lean base.
Inserted on 14 October 2026 by the operator's direction, before slice six; see the slice brief.

[x] lean-review-written — a written review of the whole lean/ tree, with findings ranked by what they cost slices six to ten (names, module structure, duplicated definitions, statement shapes, proof hygiene), and no edit.

[x] tools-read-module-sets — the model checker, the application model checker, the compiled axiom gate, the coverage inventory and the mutant harnesses read the model and the statements as a set of modules; a planted unproved statement in any module of the set fails the axiom gate and the statement manifest.

[x] big-modules-split — the model, the lemmas, the statements, the driver and the corpus runner are split into cohesive submodules, each split its own checkpoint, each a move with no change of meaning; the qualified names of protected and paper-cited statements are unchanged. The fold model's declarations are held until the other lane's change lands and move in slice eight-a.

[x] renames-and-improvements — misleading names are renamed and unidiomatic structure is repaired in at most two batches, each with its record of old and new name or move and reason; every renamed statement keeps its coverage mapping.

[x] fold-model-untouched-until-it-lands — the declarations that define or admit a fold are neither moved nor renamed before the fold admission change of another lane is on main; if the slice would otherwise idle it closes without them and they move in slice eight-a.
[x] consumers-follow — every consumer of a renamed or moved declaration is updated in the same checkpoint. (consumers-state-the-rule)

[x] rulings-listed-not-applied — findings that change a meaning, or rename a declaration main already has, or touch merged work in a way that needs a ruling, are listed with the user story of each option and not applied.
[x] regenerate-after-slice-five-b — register and digests, theorem page, simulator mirror and coverage record follow; the corpora of scenarios are byte-identical. (consumers-state-the-rule)
[x] record-five-b — the final record lists the renames (old to new), the structural moves with a reason each, the listed findings and the gate receipts.

slice-six-registrations.text: [x] failing-controls-six — a dirty request, hidden surplus, a forged syntax tag, a backdated booking and a booking wider than the maximum fail on the branch as it stands.
[x] registration-request-and-pool — the registration request, the exact-contents rule, the pending pool and the world exist.

[x] registration-booking — a booking is admitted only inside an interval no wider than the maximum, with the booked time its upper end; the syntax tag and the application tag are minted once, with the pending request.
[x] statements-six — the four supporting statements of slice six are proved.

slice-seven-terminations.text: [x] failing-controls-seven — a forged singular tag or application tag, a second pending termination and a token not in custody fail on the branch as it stands.
[x] termination-request-and-booking — the termination request and its booking exist; the token moves from custody into the request.
[x] supply-counts-pending-requests — the supply laws count tokens held by pending requests.
[x] statements-seven — statement 9 and the two supporting statements are proved.

slice-eight-a-the-fold-model-in-small-mo.text: Slice eight-a: the fold model in small modules.
Inserted on 15 October 2026 by the split of slice eight; see the slice brief. A move with no change of meaning.
[x] fold-model-move-list — a written move list names every declaration or group to move, from where to which module, the facade each file keeps and the reason, before any edit.

[x] fold-model-moved — the declarations that define or admit a fold, with the lemmas and statements that unfold them, live in cohesive modules of a few hundred lines, with the text they have on main byte for byte.

[x] fold-model-meaning-unchanged — no statement or control is added, changed or dropped; every statement keeps its fully qualified name, axiom line and digest, or the theorem page records its move; the corpora of scenarios, the transaction baseline and the driver protocol version are byte-identical.
[x] consumers-follow-eight-a — every consumer of a moved declaration follows in the same checkpoint. (consumers-state-the-rule)

slice-seven-b-the-trie-ready-tag.text: Inserted on 15 October 2026 by the operator's rulings on the trie-ready tag.
[x] failing-controls-seven-b — a termination that holds an application tag and a tag minted for another operation or nonce fail on the branch as it stands, for the intended reason.

[x] trie-ready-names — this branch's declarations built under the name syntax tag take the trie-ready names; main's names are untouched; the booking statements restate with the new vocabulary under their qualified names.

[x] termination-without-application-tag — a termination holds, mints and checks no application tag; one held is refused as dirty; the singular tag in custody stays the precondition of its trie-ready tag.
[x] tag-names-are-commitments — the application tag's name commits to the payload and a nonce and the trie-ready tag's to the operation and a nonce; one nonce per request; no injectivity is assumed.
[x] statements-seven-b — the restated booking statements are proved from the standard axioms; the list of statements carries their qualified names and axiom lines.

slice-seven-c-one-tip-number.text: Inserted on 15 October 2026 by the operator's ruling that retires the fee pin.
[x] failing-controls-seven-c — a configuration that still pins two tip numbers and a fold row that still requires the old tip cover fail on the branch as it stands.

[x] one-tip-field — the configuration carries one tip number, the minimum tip, written under the existing wire key maxFee; the preservation statements keep one pin; the chain datum and the off-chain readers are unchanged.

[x] tip-cover-retired — the old tip-cover predicate, its use in the two transaction-row statements, the tip-cover lemma and the two scenario rows about the old fee pin are retired by append-only restatement rows that name each.

[x] tip-rows-listed — the general control wrong-fee and the tip fields of the transaction baseline are listed at the first checkpoint; a live row whose expectation changes is published unmet by ruling, never as a pass; a row that keeps passing is untouched.
[x] lean-consumers-run — the consumers of a lean/ change run before the push: model check, transaction baseline, simulator, application corpus, coverage and the conformance commands without a devnet.

slice-eight-rejection-reads-the-state.text: Slice eight: rejection reads the state.

[x] failing-controls-eight — the old state-spending path, a fake, foreign or stale state, an overlapping state spend, a live member in a batch, a repeated input, a tagged request spent through the sweep arm and a rejection that carries a tag out alive fail or are refused wrongly on the branch as it stands.

[x] rejection-reads-the-state — the accepted rejection judgement exists over a transaction and goes through no fold; the evidence-bound rejection of slices two and three stays, with its statements, as the explicitly named legacy path (decision of 15 October 2026: named, not rewired).

[x] request-address-two-arms — an output lacking the trie-ready tag is spent freely, a tagged output leaves only through an exit that burns its tags in the same transaction; a rejection burns the trie-ready tag and the application tag.

[x] legacy-fold-question-retained — the driver keeps answering the old fold-with-rejection question from a retained, explicitly named legacy declaration, with scenario payloads byte-identical; nothing counts the old behaviour as meeting the ruled design.
[x] statements-eight — statements 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8 and the two supporting statements (including that a sweep leaves the pending pool and the tag supplies unchanged) are proved.

slice-eight-c-the-live-rows-published-un.text: Slice eight-c: the live rows published unmet.
Conformance and CI code, after slice eight; Codex at medium effort.

[x] live-rows-unmet-by-ruling — the live rows that exercise the old fold-with-rejection path (early rejection inside the windows, reject and retract refund controls, the running book, the generic rows) are published as unmet: "implementation follows the superseded rule; the ruled rule is not implemented".
[x] ruled-rule-tripwire — a check turns red when the deployed validators implement the ruled rule, so the unmet state cannot outlive its cause; it is proved able to fail.

slice-nine-refunds.text: [x] failing-controls-nine — a reused refund, a refund short of held minus tip and a retraction that carries a tag out alive fail on the branch as it stands.
[x] refund-obligations — rejection and retraction owe what the plan states, summed per refund address, and the registration cost comes back.
[x] statements-nine — statement 6, the second half of statement 7 and the supporting statement are proved.

slice-ten-folds.text: [ ] failing-controls-ten — a termination stranded by a fold-time check, one donation counted for many keys, a forged application tag on a registration, an unbalanced fold and a fold that carries a tag out alive fail on the branch as it stands.

[ ] fold-obligations — a registration folds inside its window and routes the cost, tip and carrier; a termination folds at any later time, burns the trie-ready tag and the singular tag and donates held minus tip, and the processor takes exactly the declared tip; a registration fold burns the trie-ready tag and the application tag and mints the singular tag at the destination.

[ ] statements-ten — statements 7 (first half), 10 (restated: only a booked termination folds, and it carries its key's genuine singular tag), 11 and 12 and the two supporting statements (including that the supply of each tag equals the count of its pending requests) are proved.
[ ] amendment-economics — the 1.18.0 entry of the constitution states the economic rows in the translation (one release, one entry).
[ ] names-and-receipts-ten — as slice five, and the full list of the thirteen statements with their status.

closing-the-ticket.text: [ ] release-record — the contract's release record is filled with the model revision, statement digests, corpus rows, constitution version and remaining limits. (consumers-state-the-rule)

[ ] pull-request-body — the body states the story, the exact model revision, the mapping from requirement to statement to check, and the limits: no validator, no builder, no live acceptance. (unmet-stays-unmet)
